sec: Progression table, follow-up conversions, chronic hepatitis profile, mutants, serological patterns table

items.q: Progression table — match — 1) Recovery 2) Chronic hepatitis 3) AFH with simple HBV infection 4) AFH with HBV + HDV co-infection … A) 5–20% B) 0.1–1% C) 95–99% D) 1–5%
items.exp: Recovery 95–99%; Chronic hepatitis 1–5%; Acute fulminant hepatitis: simple HBV 0.1–1%, HBV + HDV coinfection 5–20%. (Book p1038)

items.q: Follow-up is done after how long, per the printed bullet?
opts: 24 weeks since IP / 12–16 weeks of symptom onset
6 weeks since IP / 2 weeks of symptoms
24 weeks of symptom onset / 12–16 weeks since IP
items.exp: 'After 24 weeks since IP/12–16 wks of symptom onset'. (Book p1038)

items.q: Follow-up conversions — match — 1) HBsAg 2) Anti-HBc IgG 3) HBeAg … A) converts to anti-HBeAg B) converts to anti-HBsAg C) converts to anti-HBc IgM (as printed)
items.exp: Printed: 'HBsAg converts→ anti HBsAg; Anti HBc IgG converts→ Anti HBc IgM; HBeAg → anti HBeAg' — all three bracketed as Recovery. (Note: the printed IgG→IgM direction is the reverse of the usual IgM→IgG class switch; taught here as written.) (Book p1038)

items.q: Per the follow-up bullet, which serological pair defines chronic hepatitis?
items.exp: 'HBsAg +ve, anti HBc IgG +ve : Chronic hepatitis'. (Book p1038)

items.q: Chronic hepatitis profile: HBsAg + and anti-HBc IgG +; HBeAg is POSITIVE. What HBV DNA threshold and interpretation does the flowchart give?
opts: HBV DNA load > 20,000 IU/mL — high infectivity, high replication
HBV DNA load > 2,000 IU/mL — high infectivity, high replication
HBV DNA load < 2,000 IU/mL — low infectivity, carrier state
HBV DNA at any level — carrier, no need of Rx but HCC risk
items.exp: '+ve → HBV DNA load > 20000 IU/mL → High infectivity, high replication'. (Book p1038)

items.q: HBeAg NEGATIVE branch — match — 1) HBV DNA > 2,000 IU/mL 2) HBV DNA < 2,000 IU/mL … A) Low infectivity, low replication → carriers B) High infectivity, high replication
items.exp: HBeAg −ve: HBV DNA > 2000 → high infectivity/replication; < 2000 → low infectivity/replication → Carriers. (Book p1038)

items.q: Carriers (HBeAg −, DNA < 2000) — judge: I No need of Rx. II No risk for HCC.
items.exp: 'Carriers → No need of Rx; Risk for HCC.' (Book p1038)

items.q: Pre-core / basal core mutant carries a very poor prognosis with ↑ risk for three outcomes. Which is NOT listed?
items.exp: 'Pre-Core / Basal Core mutant : very poor prognosis; ↑ risk for HCC, Cirrhosis, Decompensation.' (Book p1038)

items.q: Serological patterns table — match — 1) HBsAg + / anti-HBs − / anti-HBc IgM / HBeAg + / anti-HBe − 2) HBsAg + / anti-HBs − / anti-HBc IgG / HBeAg + / anti-HBe − … A) Chronic hepatitis B, high infectivity B) Acute hepatitis B, high infectivity
items.exp: Row 1: acute hepatitis B, high infectivity (IgM). Row 2: chronic hepatitis B, high infectivity (IgG). (Book p1038)

items.q: Serology: HBsAg +, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe −. Give the two printed interpretations and the confirmatory step.
opts: Late acute or chronic hepatitis B with low infectivity, OR HBeAg-negative (precore-mutant) hepatitis B — do HBV DNA to confirm
Window period of seroconversion from HBsAg to anti-HBs, OR heterotypic anti-HBs — repeat anti-HBs in 4 weeks
Recovery from hepatitis B, OR hepatitis B in the remote past — no further test is needed
Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B, OR escape mutant — do anti-HBc IgM to confirm
items.exp: Row 3: '1. Late acute or chronic hepatitis B, low infectivity 2. HBeAg negative (Precore-mutant) hepatitis B (Chronic or, rarely, acute). Do HBV DNA to confirm'. (Book p1038)

items.q: Serology: HBsAg +, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc +, HBeAg ±, anti-HBe ±. Which pair of interpretations is printed, and which is labelled common vs rare?
opts: HBsAg of one subtype with heterotypic anti-HBs (common); seroconversion from HBsAg to anti-HBs in progress (rare, window period)
Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B (common); S-gene escape mutant that fails to express HBsAg (rare)
Recovery from hepatitis B with persisting antigenaemia (common); hepatitis B in the remote past (rare)
Immunisation with HBsAg vaccine plus passive HBIG (common); occult HBV with low viral load (rare)
items.exp: Row 4: '1. HBsAg of one subtype and heterotypic anti-HBs (common) 2. Process of seroconversion from HBsAg to anti HBs (rare) (window period)'. (Book p1038)

items.q: Serology: HBsAg −, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgM, HBeAg ±, anti-HBe ±. Interpretation?
opts: Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B
items.exp: Row 5: 'Acute reactivation of chronic hepatitis B'. (Book p1038)

items.q: Last three rows — match — 1) HBsAg −, anti-HBs −, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe ± 2) HBsAg −, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc IgG, HBeAg −, anti-HBe ± 3) HBsAg −, anti-HBs +, anti-HBc −, HBeAg −, anti-HBe − … A) Recovery from hepatitis B B) Immunisation with HBsAg (after vaccination) C) Hepatitis B in remote past, or escape mutant
items.exp: Row 6: remote past / escape mutant (anti-HBc alone). Row 7: recovery (anti-HBs + anti-HBc). Row 8: immunisation (anti-HBs alone). (Book p1038)

items.q: Which single-marker pattern distinguishes vaccination from natural recovery in the serological table?
opts: Anti-HBc is absent after vaccination but present after recovery
Anti-HBe is present after vaccination but absent after recovery
items.exp: Immunisation row: anti-HBs + with anti-HBc −; recovery row: anti-HBs + with anti-HBc IgG. (Book p1038)
